speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Could you please describe the skin lesions you are concerned about, including when they first appeared and if they are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the papules flesh-colored or red, and do you see any central indentation or umbilication in the center of the lesions? Also, has the child had any recent fever or respiratory symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of flesh-colored, pearly papules with central umbilication is classic for Molluscum Contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum
